_note: Terrain grid for the Western Canada (CPR, 1881-87) map. 40 cols x 34 rows, pointy-top odd-r, hex radius 24. Grid dimensions: this board's real city footprint spans ~28 degrees of longitude (Nanaimo to Selkirk) but only ~5.1 degrees of latitude (Victoria to Edmonton) — the opposite proportion from the Canadian 1851 board's 24.5 x ~6.65-degree footprint. 40 columns give enough east-west resolution to keep the whole prairie corridor legible at this hex size; 34 rows (well beyond the ~22 rows a literal isotropic projection would need) exist because project.mjs deliberately over-stretches the latitude scale (rowsPerDegLat 4.6 vs an isotropic ~0.9) so that tight real-world clusters — Fort Qu'Appelle/Qu'Appelle Station, Golden/Field, Winnipeg/St. Boniface, the Lower Mainland triangle, Victoria/Esquimalt — land in distinguishable rows instead of colliding outright; see project.mjs's own header comment. The grid was generated (scripts/western/gen-terrain.mjs, kept for reference/regeneration) from a hand-specified route network mirroring the real CPR mainline and its branches, then hand-reviewed. Legend: O = off-map (water, wilderness, or panel space), P = plains, F = forest, M = mountain, C = city (the city itself comes from cities.json, which must place a city on every C — see build-map.mjs, which stamps 'terrain:city' over whatever base letter is here; the letter only has to not be 'O').

regions._note: Why each area is the terrain it is. Purely documentation — the generator reads only `grid`.
regions.Northern boreal arc: Rows 0-9. Forest. The Edmonton/Battleford/Prince Albert branch sits up here, off the CPR mainline proper — matching the research doc's note that this band saw very little of the real 1881-87 construction story and should read as sparse, low-value scenery, same choice as the Canadian board's Shield interior.
regions.Rockies and Selkirks chokepoint: Roughly cols 8-19, rows 10-19. Mountain. Banff, Field, Golden, Revelstoke and the Kicking Horse/Rogers Pass corridor — the single hardest and most expensive stretch of the whole railway, per the research doc's terrain section.
regions.Fraser Canyon / BC interior plateau: Cols 0-8, rows 14-19. Mountain, shading toward plains near Kamloops. Onderdonk's Fraser Canyon contract (Yale) and the drier interior plateau country the Thompson River corridor crosses.
regions.Lower Mainland / Fraser lowlands: Cols 0-7, rows 19-25. Plains. Vancouver, Port Moody, New Westminster and Yale's western end — flat lowland delta country opening onto the Strait of Georgia.
regions.Vancouver Island water gap: Cols 0-7, rows 24-26 are almost entirely off-map — the Strait of Georgia. A single narrow line of land hexes (col 1-2, rows 24-26) is the only crossing between the mainland cluster and Nanaimo, mirroring how the Canadian board's Charlottetown/Pictou and Sydney/Cape Breton crossings work: mostly a real off-map water gap, with one deliberately narrow, game-abstracted land link so the whole map stays one connected landmass. See the Vancouver Island section of the build report for the reasoning.
regions.Vancouver Island: Cols 0-6, rows 25-33. Plains near Nanaimo/Victoria/Esquimalt, forest further south — Victoria, Esquimalt and Nanaimo's own landmass, reached only via the crossing above and, in reality, never by the CPR itself (the Esquimalt & Nanaimo Railway was a separate, independently-owned company in this era).
regions.Prairie corridor: Everything else with cols >= 13 roughly (Manitoba, Saskatchewan/Assiniboia, and Alberta east of the foothills). Plains — the flat-to-rolling country that let Van Horne's crews lay 500+ miles in a single season (1882).
